summary: Ryotai Shibuya was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.

Ryoun Yamada is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied under Yamada Koun and attended Harvard Business School. He worked at Mitsubishi Bank (~1964–1996), Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi (~1996–1999), and became Leiter at Sanbo Zen in 2004.

Ryudo Fujii studied Indology and philosophy under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1953–1955). He spent his academic career at Rissho University as a lecturer (~1961–1970), associate professor (~1970–1978), professor (~1978–2001), and president (~1992–1998).

Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. His affiliations include posts at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014), and Taisho University as a specially appointed associate professor (attested 2014–2018).

Ryuichi Abe studied at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia universities under mentors including Yoshito S. Hakeda and Philip Boas Yampolsky. A scholar of Buddhist, Japanese, and religious studies, he held professorships at Columbia (1998–2004) and Harvard (~2003).
Ryukai Mano was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He succeeded Yuishin Ito and served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1991).
Ryuken Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2014, he was attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Ryusei Keira works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his thesis at the University of Lausanne by 2003 under the doctoral supervision of Tom Tillemans.

Ryushin Uryuzu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University (~1951–1955). He worked at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute (attested 1962) and served as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1969–1998).
Ryusho Onami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taishun Mibu. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1985).
Ryuta Kikutani works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as a specialist researcher at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and at Kyoto University (attested 2020).

Ryutaro Tsuchida studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo and the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau. He was an assistant at Marburg (~1981–1983) and later served as professor and professor emeritus (1995–2012) at Tokyo.
Ryō Nishimura specialized in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1995) and under Fumihiko Sueki (~1996–2004).
Ryōshū Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daishun Ueyama. He held a lecturing post at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Ryūjō Yamada studied at Tokyo Imperial University and under Sylvain Lévi in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held appointments at Ryukoku University (~1925–1946) and served as a professor at Tohoku University (~1946–1958).

Ryūshō Hikata studied Indology and Buddhist studies under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor and dean at Kyushu University and president of Fukuoka Women's University (1960–1964).
Ryūzan Nishimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.
Ryūō Asahi was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Tō-ji (as Sōgaku) and at Koyasan University.
Rüdiger Schmitt is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1958–1965) and served on the faculty at Saarland University (~1972–2004).
